messages:
maria: Heads-up — after last night's CUDA 13.2 + driver 535 rollout in us-west2 we started seeing sporadic hangs in multi-GPU inference pools. Investigating.

raj: I saw several jobs stuck on allreduce. nvtop shows GPUs fully occupied but NCCL progress stops. No immediate OOMs. Any core dumps yet?

sasha: I grabbed logs from node gpu-uf-21. Repeating pattern: "NCCL WARN Call to net->listen timed out" then "ncclReduceScatter timeout" around 10:42 UTC. Snippet below.

oliver: ```[2026-03-17 10:42:12] NCCL WARN Call to net->listen timed out after 30s
[2026-03-17 10:42:12] NCCL INFO Using collNet
[2026-03-17 10:42:13] NCCL ERROR Allreduce failed: timeout
[2026-03-17 10:42:13] CUDA Kernel completed with status 0x7 (timeout)
```

anya: @maria is this limited to racks with HDR RDMA on? We also deployed kernel 6.6 + firmware on a subset last night.

infra-bot: DeployBot: Driver 535.86 rolled to us-west2 pool (canary 20%).

maria: Good catch — failure surface does match RDMA-enabled racks. Non-RDMA racks show higher latencies but don't hang. That points at net plugin / mlx5 interaction with the new kernel/driver combo.

raj: Repro steps I ran: stress-collective --gpus=4 --iters=5000. With NCCL 2.14.3 I get ~60% runs clean, ~40% hang between iter 1800-2200.

sasha: We validated NCCL 2.14.3 + driver 520.x on k6.4 kernels locally and didn't hit this. So likely a regression introduced by either kernel 6.6 or driver 535 with RDMA path.

oliver: Short-term mitigation: set NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1 on the inference fleet to force fallback to TCP (avoids RDMA path). That will increase token latency and CPU/NET usage but should prevent hangs. Can we push an env override via rollout?

maria: We should. Patch the inference-low-latency service with an env override and restart agents. Be mindful of cost — TCP fallback increases per-token egress and CPU handling. Rough back-of-envelope: ~22% higher cost for affected endpoints.

anya: Another option: try NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1 and NCCL_P2P_LEVEL=SYS to get graceful aborts and better dumps; if that fails we rollback driver on a small rack.

raj: I'll enable NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1 and NCCL_DEBUG_SUBSYS=COLL on one canary host to capture better traces. Also collecting tcpdump and rdma dumps.

sasha: dmesg on gpu-uf-21 also shows repeated mlx5_core messages: "mlx5_core: QP timeout, hw qpn 0x3f" matching the NCCL timeouts. Saving kernel ring and /var/log/messages.

maria: Action items: (1) Toggle NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1 in staging canary (10%) now. (2) Rollback driver to 520.x on one RDMA rack for a controlled test. (3) Collect full core dumps + rdma logs and open ticket with Mellanox/driver team if confirmed. (4) Produce brief cost/impact note for PM/ops.

oliver: I'll take the config rollout. Initiating: config id cfg-20260317-rc7 -> targeting inference-low-latency canary=10% now.

infra-bot: Config rollout started: cfg-20260317-rc7 -> 10% -> inference-low-latency.

maria: Perfect. If SLAs start to degrade we'll escalate to emergency infra sync. React with :warning: :hourglass_flowing_sand: for visibility.

anya: One more datapoint — eu-west1 had a partial driver holdback and shows no hangs. That reinforces the hypothesis.

raj: Will post collected traces and a short reproduction doc once uploads complete.

sasha: Uploaded rdma logs to s3://redwood-infra/debug/nccl-535-hang/gpu-uf-21.tar.gz. Link: https://s3.redwood/internal/nccl-535-hang/gpu-uf-21.tar.gz

maria: Thanks all — keeping this thread as single source of truth. Next update after canary results or rollback test.
